proof.criterion: A1 — with the listener's session cache emptied and refilling and the session's record in the store, a Dispatch comment mention of that session is delivered.
proof.surface: Real binaries, built at the code head: two `cmd/listener` processes (A, which Dispatch's ENVOY_URL names, and B) on one real nats-server with JetStream; the real `cmd/dispatch` server on a real Postgres 16 with pgvector; a fake agent endpoint for each session, recording every frame pushed to /session/<id>/prompt_async. The cold cache comes from the hub-rebuild sequence and not from a test hook: the KV_envoy_sessions stream is deleted, B restarts and creates the bucket again, and the sessions register again through B. A's session watcher is not rebuilt until its next 30 s self-health tick, so A's cache does not hold them.
proof.command: /legion/scratch/tmp/tester/run/up.sh ./dispatch-head && /legion/scratch/tmp/tester/run/cold.sh h1   (cold.sh: delete KV_envoy_sessions with the nats client, restart listener B, POST B/v1/interests/subscribe for ses_h1_planner and ses_h1_tester, then POST /api/v1/issues/TST-1/comments with mentions [{target: session:ses_h1_planner}], delivery steer, and POST /api/v1/broadcasts)
proof.observed: Before the Dispatch calls, A's `GET /v1/sessions` held neither session (`A list holds: []`) and A's `GET /v1/registry/ses_h1_tester` answered 200 with session_id, title, capabilities and host. The mention's attempt was `{"session_id":"ses_h1_planner","state":"sent","error":null}`. ses_h1_planner's own endpoint received the frame `[NOTIFICATION to you from dispatch] … Mention h1`.
proof.negativeControl: The same rig and script, with the Dispatch binary built from envoy_resolve.go, broadcasts.go and issue_claim.go of 410a7b543c3b (`up.sh ./dispatch-old && cold.sh o1`). A's list was again empty, and the mention was `{"session_id":null,"state":"failed","error":"no live session ses_o1_planner"}`. No frame reached ses_o1_planner. This is the defect, reproduced through the hub-rebuild path on real binaries.

proof.criterion: A2 — a broadcast to several sessions in the same state reaches all of them.
proof.surface: The same real-binary rig and hub-rebuild sequence. Up to 100 sessions re-register through listener B while Dispatch asks listener A.
proof.command: cold.sh h1 (a broadcast to ses_h1_planner and ses_h1_tester), then cold100.sh k2 (delete the bucket, restart B, register ses_k2_001…ses_k2_100 through B, then POST /api/v1/broadcasts with all 100 session_ids)
proof.observed: Two sessions: `201 {"recipients":["ses_h1_planner","ses_h1_tester"],"excluded":[]}`, and both endpoints received the broadcast frame. 100 sessions: A's list held 0 of the 100 before the send; the broadcast answered `201` in 0.26 s with recipients 100 and excluded 0; 100 frames carrying the body reached the endpoint. At the cap boundary, 101 selected sessions answer `400 BROADCAST_INPUT a broadcast reaches at most 100 sessions (101 selected)`, and one session named twice gives one recipient.
proof.negativeControl: With the pre-change Dispatch binary (cold.sh o1), the broadcast answered `201 {"recipients":["ses_o1_tester"],"excluded":[{"session_id":"ses_o1_planner","reason":"no live session"}]}`. The planner was excluded. The tester was a recipient only because the script's own per-session read had warmed A's cache for it, which the old resolution then found in the list.

proof.criterion: A3 — a session that genuinely has no record is still refused, with the same words as today.
proof.surface: The real listener binary's /v1/registry route, and the real Dispatch binary asking it. Also the head Dispatch binary asking a pre-change listener binary (api.go of 410a7b543c3b), which is the order of a rollout that deploys Dispatch first.
proof.command: curl A/v1/registry/<id> for ses_never, a.b, a%2Fb, a..b, a%20b, ses:bad, ünï, *, >, a 300-character id, and a DELETE; then a comment mentioning session:ses_compat and session:ses_nobody, and a broadcast to both, through Dispatch(head) → listener(pre-change)
proof.observed: `ses_never` → `404 {"error":"no live session ses_never"}`. `a.b` and `a/b` → 404 with the same words. `a..b`, `a b`, `ses:bad`, `ünï`, `*` and `>` → 400, with no Retry-After. DELETE → 405, and an empty id → 400. Through Dispatch, ses_nobody's mention attempt was `failed` with `no live session ses_nobody`, and the broadcast excluded it with reason `no live session`. Against the pre-change listener, the head Dispatch still delivered the mention to ses_compat (`state: sent`, and the frame arrived) and still refused ses_nobody with the same words. The old route's raw entry (no session_id, no host) decodes correctly.
proof.negativeControl: A registered session in the same run (`ses_live`) answers 200 with its row, so the 404 depends on the record. The browser spec `a mention of a session the listener holds no record of is still refused as no live session` passes in both the chromium and the iphone projects.

proof.criterion: A4 — a read that does not answer is refused as a temporary condition, not as an absence.
proof.surface: The real-binary rig with nats-server SIGSTOPped (connections stay open and nothing answers). Separately, with listener A SIGSTOPped.
proof.command: /legion/scratch/tmp/tester/run/stall.sh: kill -STOP <nats-server>; curl A/v1/registry/ses_stall_cold; a mention of session:ses_stall_cold; a broadcast to [ses_stall_live, ses_stall_cold] with idempotency_key stall-key; kill -CONT, then the same broadcast key again. Then kill -STOP <listener A> and a broadcast and a mention.
proof.observed: The NATS stall: the route answered `503 {"error":"envoy: the message bus did not answer: read session ses_stall_cold from the bucket: context deadline exceeded"}` with `Retry-After: 1` in 2.00 s. A session in A's cache still answered 200 in 1 ms. The mention's attempt was failed, session_id null, error `envoy listener: GET /v1/registry/ses_stall_cold returned 503: envoy: the message bus did not answer: …`, which does not begin `no live session `. The broadcast was `503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE` in 2.0 s, and `select count(*) from broadcasts` did not change. After SIGCONT, the same idempotency key was accepted fresh (`recipients [ses_stall_live]`, and ses_stall_cold, which has no record, was excluded `no live session`), so the key was left free. The frozen listener: the broadcast was `503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE` at 5.007 s with nothing written, and the mention failed with `envoy listener: GET /v1/registry/ses_live: … context deadline exceeded`.
proof.negativeControl: The same reads after SIGCONT answer 200 for a registered session and 404 `no live session` for one with no record. The browser spec `a mention of a session the listener could not read is refused with the listener's reason, not as no live session` fails against the pre-change resolution and passes at head in chromium and iphone.

proof.criterion: A5 (plan D10) — a working session's issue claim is not taken while the cache refills, a gone holder's claim is free, and a read that does not answer takes nothing.
proof.surface: The real-binary rig: POST /api/v1/issues/<key>/claim with the agent bearer, the body `dispatch claim` sends.
proof.command: cold100.sh k2 (ses_k2_100 claims TST-3 while A's list lacks it, then ses_contender_k2 claims); the stall run (ses_ghost, which never registered, claims TST-2; the contender claims while NATS is SIGSTOPped, and again after SIGCONT)
proof.observed: Cold holder: A's list did not hold ses_k2_100 (`false`). The contender got `409 ISSUE_CLAIMED session ses_k2_100 (N100) claimed this issue …`, with the title from the holder's own record. Stalled bus: the contender got `503 ENVOY_UNAVAILABLE … GET /v1/registry/ses_ghost returned 503: envoy: the message bus did not answer` in 2.0 s, and the claim was not taken. After SIGCONT: ses_ghost has no record, and the contender took the claim (holder now ses_contender).
proof.negativeControl: The pre-change claim code is in the Dispatch build of the cross-service control above. There, TestDispatchRefusesAClaimTakeoverWhileTheCacheRefills fails because the cold holder's claim is granted to the contender.

Only the comment is wrong, and it is on a line whose behaviour depends on a string prefix.

Not a failure; for the reviewer. resolveBroadcastSessions breaks out of its loop when groupCtx.Err() is set. If the five-second budget ends in the gap between one group.Go and the next check, and every read already launched has succeeded, group.Wait returns nil. The unread ids would then be excluded as `no live session`, which is the stored exclusion D7 forbids. I found no deterministic way to reach this: a slot that is waiting launches its read on the expired context, and that read fails. The window is the instant between two loop iterations. A check of ctx.Err() after Wait would close it.
